title: Grateful Dead Live at Electric Factory on 1969-02-15
lineage: SBD > MR > Cassette > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording with solid vintage clarity captures a high‑energy 1969 show, highlighted by a soaring Dark Star, monster The Other One and an incendiary Alligator > Caution sequence.
ai_review.review: The performance is praised for its intense jams – Dark Star, The Other One, Eleven, Mountains of the Moon and the Alligator>Caution stretch are repeatedly called out as stand‑outs.  Recording quality is described as good for the era (soundboard tape), though a few cuts in the middle of the show hurt the flow.  Overall the show feels high‑energy and historically significant.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4–5 stars and extol the musical peaks, while a handful note cuts and occasional tuning issues; recording is judged good for its vintage source, yielding an overall rating just under 4.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear vintage tape sound – “good audio quality for the period”. Some reviewers note noticeable cuts (especially in Eleven/Death Don't) and occasional tuning hiccups, but no major distortion or dropout.

poor_songs: Death Don't Have To Be So Bad (cut)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Reviewers emphasize a powerful second set with seamless transitions, especially the Alligator‑Caution jam; cuts interrupt some moments but overall pacing is described as intense and flowing.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for searing, confident guitar work and strong vocal delivery – “Jerry’s voice is primed”, “Jerry ripping it up”, “searing…pure and divine”.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for solid bass interplay, especially during the Dark Star jam (“beautiful rhythmic conversation between guitars and Phil”).
band_member_comments.Keys: Organ highlighted as “great organ playing” on Dark Star; keyboards contribute to the psychedelic texture.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drums receive strong compliments – “the Drums…pure and Divine”, cowbell presence, intense driving rhythm throughout.
